_comment: Messages this server defines on top of the client's own table.

An entry whose id already exists is an OVERRIDE: it replaces the retail name, text and arity rather than being appended. That is how a message gains a parameter — retexting 139 to carry a chance also renames it, because the C<n>/S<n> tokens in the name are what fix the constructor's arity.

Overrides are used here in preference to inventing ids. New ids did not render at all: 9000 (far past the end of the table) and 7491 (immediately after it) both produced nothing, whatever the row's colour, group or type said. Something outside SystemMsg*.dat evidently decides which ids the client will accept, so reusing rows it already accepts is the reliable route.
Numbering is the parameter order the packet carries, not the order the tokens read in the sentence.

messages.name: C1_HAS_RESISTED_YOUR_S2_CHANCE_S3
messages.note: Retail 'C1_HAS_RESISTED_YOUR_S2' ($c1 has resisted your $s2.), retexted to carry the computed landing chance.

messages.name: S1_HAS_SUCCEEDED_ON_C2_CHANCE_S3
messages.note: Retail 'S1_HAS_SUCCEEDED' ($s1 has succeeded.), retexted as the success half of the same roll.
